intended_object: From the docstring and context: the diagram (functor) WalkingMulticospan J ⥤ C built from multicospan index data. It sends the left vertex `a` to `I.left a` and the right vertex `b` to `I.right b`. The two generating arrows into `right b` go to `I.fst b` and `I.snd b`. A multiequalizer is then defined as the limit of this diagram.
explanation: The definition is faithful; this is Mathlib's own canonical construction, so there is no separate Mathlib counterpart to cite. On objects it sends `left a` to `I.left a` and `right b` to `I.right b`. On morphisms it sends identities to identities, and the generating arrows `fst b : left (J.fst b) ⟶ right b` and `snd b : left (J.snd b) ⟶ right b` to `I.fst b` and `I.snd b`, whose types match. The walking category has no nontrivial composites, so the functor laws hold (the proof handles them). The definition works for an arbitrary shape J and an arbitrary category C, which is its full natural generality.
